Messages.Author: Cry Wolf
Messages.Body:
LSJ,

I think many in our playgroup misinterpret Forced Awakening. From the
threads that came up with the search terms "forced awakening
author:LSJ", it seems apparent that if a vamp plays FA, he/she *must*
attempt to block. If the attempt fails, then the vamp burns a blood.
(card text)

In addition, if the vamp plays FA then merely misdirects a bleed,
he/she burns a blood for FA too.

Furthermore, a vamp cannot play FA then _not_ attempt to block (just to
cycle cards) and in so doing *not* burn a blood. (In the card text,
it's reading "can" as an option, not as a capacity that must be taken.)

It is now very clear why Wake has a place in non-wallish decks, since
FA has a glaring penalty! So the deciding factor between WWEF and FA is
not simply the "Do not replace" clause, but also the requirement to
attempt to block (and the corresponding penalty if it fails)!

Am I correct? Or is my moment of nirvana about to be shattered by the
power-that-is, who utters monosyllabic affirmations and rejections?

FA Card text:
This reacting vampire _can_ attempt to block and play reaction cards as
though untapped. If he or she does not successfully block this action,
he or she burns an additional blood.

/Cry Wolf

Messages.Author: Jozxyqk
Messages.Body:
Cry Wolf <gsa...@gmail.com> wrote:
> LSJ,

> I think many in our playgroup misinterpret Forced Awakening. From the
> threads that came up with the search terms "forced awakening
> author:LSJ", it seems apparent that if a vamp plays FA, he/she *must*
> attempt to block. If the attempt fails, then the vamp burns a blood.
> (card text)

That's wrong.
You can play Forced Awakening and *not* block.
It just says that if you don't block, you burn a blood.
Card text does not say "This vampire *attempts to* block". It says
"can".

The latter. (That's three syllables! Monosyllabism is hard to achieve when given
